t: Bosses: Ushan, Rottenfang, Cobweb Spider, Shadow, Zinovy Gorsky.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by vampires.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. You know what happened in the Darkblood Citadel. The ancestral nest of the House de Doucer, where all high society once flocked to balls and soirées, turned into a nest of ghouls. Armando de Doucer got in league with Tep and staged a vampire invasion of Kania and Avilon. Only the intervention of heroes like you thwarted his plans... But what if everything had gone differently? Do you know who the worst enemies of vampires are? Werewolves! It seems to have something to do with the blood curse that lies on both of them. If the spires of a galleon palace appear in the mysterious astral, get ready to see what would have happened if the werewolves had got to the ghouls before the heroes of the League. Only don't let your guard down: werewolves hate the likes of you only a little less than bloodsuckers. Mind you don't end up between the hammer and the anvil!

Bosses: Ushan, Rottenfang, Webweaver, Shadow, Zinovy Gorsky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Wormfaces.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. An ancient temple of a vanished people... To whom did they offer prayers in it? To the One Creator? To local spirits? To great heroes and rulers? What did they sacrifice — incense or someone's hearts? Today no one knows. The temple ruins on Gipat became the stage for the last act of the Play, where the heroes of Sarnaut received the Revelation. I was there too... Now that's a place I'd rather not go back to! But one traveler told me that in the depths of the mysterious astral he saw a reflection of the June Temple: ruins where imps and demon worshippers wander. True, in that temple the cultists dug up some June magitech and are now at war with it, not knowing how to bury it again. He also let slip that at the very end the temple gave him an unpleasant surprise. If you ask me — what could be more unpleasant than what we actually found in it? But you, if you find this reflection, keep your ears open!

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t: Bosses: Mikhail Blankstare, Artem Ostankin, George Podpalin, Hungry Demon, Megalit.

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. The name of Tep no longer strikes terror into peaceful folk. This ancient Hickutian sorcerer, who longed to become a god, was destroyed by the heroes of the Empire on the shards of the allod of Irdrich, with some minor help from the brave souls of the League. But what if Tep had not been resurrected? What would have become of his lair if it had never seen its master return? They say that in the depths of the astral one can find a reflection of Irdrich where there is neither a pyramid nor cultists — only the grim inventions of the ancient necromancer, which go on wrecking ships and snuffing out Sparks even without their creator. If you come across this place, be careful: though it is only what might have happened, Tep's reflected machines are no less dangerous than the real ones!

Bosses: Mikhail Blankstare, Artem Ostankin, George Podpalin, Hungry Demon, Megalit.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t: Bosses: Armando de Doucer, Poisonous Trap, Darksoul Leader, Purger Fire Thrower, Meat Golem.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a laboratory is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Secret laboratories... The Committee can stamp as many secrecy classifications as it likes, but murder will out: even the lowliest goblin under a fence already knows that our research program has serious problems. Something explodes in one laboratory, something leaks in another, and in a third the head of the lab turns out to be a cultist. And the harder they try to classify it all, the more rumors go around. And rumors have a power of their own. Because the astral... The astral knows how to listen. And now in its depths you can find a reflection that embodies all the scary tales about Imperial laboratories. Mad scientists, cultist spies, inhuman experiments, nightmarish machines and mutilated test subjects — everything idle chatterboxes might spin for you. So if you see a science town behind iron gates somewhere in the astral and decide to go ashore... I hope you have strong nerves!

Bosses: Armando de Doucer, Poisonous Trap, Darksoul Leader, Purger Fire Thrower, Meat Golem.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t: Bosses: Trap, Asyka, Marcel de Doucer, Daring Family, Miroslav Kramolsky.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: League allod; a prison is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Don't you really know about this place? Although... you probably have no need to. Oreshek Fortress is the largest and most impregnable prison in the whole League. They hold the most dangerous cutthroats and butchers there, thieves and swindlers, traitors and rebels. No one has ever escaped from there — where would you run to from an astral island! They say the Committee tried to carry out a special operation there: to free some dangerous rebel and drop him back onto Kania — let Aidenus have a headache. The guards turned out to be no slouches, and our people barely got away... But that's in reality! And somewhere in the depths of the astral a reflection has appeared in which the prisoner got free. And, you know, those who have seen that reflection say it's a good thing the Committee didn't succeed in reality. Unpatriotic, of course, but the last thing we needed was one of the League's mightiest fortresses turned into a bandit nest!

Bosses: Trap, Asyka, Marcel de Doucer, Daring Family, Miroslav Kramolsky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t: Bosses: Vissarion Arhivin, Yasskul Ktash, Astral Overlord, Gorluxor, Demon of Decay.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Is it for me to tell you about Tensess Temple! After all, it was you who had to fight your way through hordes of enemies to uncover the secret of the gift of Light. I'd like to know what you heroes saw there and what the Spark of Tensess told you. But a state secret is a state secret. I'd better tell you what I know about its astral reflection.

A half-ruined sanctuary in the depths of the jungle — the tomb of an ancient mage, a rival of Nezeb himself. You won't find the Spark of Tensess in the reflection, but there will be enemies in abundance. In this the reflection is very close to reality... You'll have to overcome the most dangerous enemies and a whole horde of demons at the very top of the temple. But the reward will be worthy! Who knows, perhaps the reflection will share new secrets with you?

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: Elven allod, a settlement of the House de Doucer.

Story:

We are met by Patrick de Doucer. He tells us that all those who did not follow Armando have gathered on this allod. The other elven houses would not accept them, and they want nothing to do with the vampires. Patrick asks us to help win back the southern part of the allod from the creatures living there. First, to defeat the granite trolls and their leader, Cliff. Martin de Doucer also has a request for us, but this time to help on the eastern part of the allod. Mantises live there, and it is them we must deal with. The Great Mage Karl de Doucer turns to us. He tells us that for the time being he is protecting the allod from the astral and holding up the shields; he is worried by the presence of lizards on the allod — they are far more dangerous than any trolls or mantises. The lizards are ruled by a creature resembling a draconid, named Oskal. The trouble is that he can't be negotiated with, as with the lizards, and our goal is to make our way into their settlement and destroy Oskal. After clearing the allod of the mantises and trolls, we go to the lizards' altar. There we defeat Oskal. The sentries Patrick and Martin thank us and say that now developing the settlement will be easier. And the Great Mage thanks us and says that he now feels better, since the evil that was hindering him has been defeated.

Bosses: Troll Chief Cliff, Lizard Leader Oskal.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
It resembles Tenebra.

We meet the Elf Scius de Desirae. He tells us that there is a copy of the Galleon Castle here, which has slipped out of control and turned against the elves in its rage. He asks us to help destroy the elementals. After defeating them we return to the Elf. He thanks us for the help and gives us the "Ring of the Eight Houses", which was supposed to continue the story... But nothing further is known.

[Map missing]

Climate: Varied (temperate and tundra), closest to Tenebra and Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, although representatives of the House de Desirae have settled here.

Story:

After landing on the allod, we are met by the master seeker Scius de Desirae.

According to him, their House was building a galleon ship, but decided to secretly build another ship for personal purposes; however, it rebelled and vanished. They searched for it carefully while concealing what they were doing, and in the end found it wrecked on this allod. We are asked to try to tame it (the galleon). By killing the elementals, we show the galleon our strength. We return to Scius; he thanks us for the help and gives us the ring of the 8 houses, which was supposed to continue the story, but there is no information about it.

Bosses: Great Fire Elemental, Great Water Elemental, Great Ice Elemental, Great Air Elemental.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Ugh, what a question! Rotswamp is the vilest place in the astral. It squelches underfoot, drips down your collar, insects swarm in the mud, and the fog is so thick you can't see your own feet. In short, Rotswamp is the vilest bog in the world! And how many travellers have perished there... Wherever you go, you run straight into dangerous creatures!

When I had the bad luck to end up in that stinking bog with an expedition, on the very first day we lost three guards in fights with hydras. Terrible, venom-spitting creatures — and the oldest hydra, which we nicknamed Echidna, bit a pack horse in half in a single snap!

At night we woke to horrible screams: lamias armed to the teeth had attacked the camp, cut down the sentry and rushed at us, shouting something about two sisters thirsting for our blood. We barely fought them off!

But as we retreated, we went deep into the heart of the bog, and that is where the main danger lay in wait for us. We had barely had time to wonder why the lamias had stopped chasing us when a huge drake dived out of the night sky straight onto our party, pouring fire over everything around, while smaller drakes circled overhead to make sure none of us escaped. I survived only by a miracle — I fell into the mud, burrowed into it, and the drakes did not notice me. My comrades were not so lucky...

By morning, having waited until the drakes finished their bloody feast and flew away, I crept back to the ship. Utterly exhausted, wounded and covered in mud from head to toe, at the sight of the ship waiting for us I almost wept with relief, and I swore I would never set foot in that accursed place again!

Bosses: Echidna, Euriala and Stheno, Old Swamper, Venomwing.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lamias and drakes.

t: Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's not to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with the technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they wanted to open the gates, I don't know, and where they did open them, I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the staff were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. Want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you do love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... well, maybe just in a low voice, in my ear.

Ney is not a very large allod, although it was here that Zayan, together with Skrakan, first succeeded in creating the holding ritual. It lies in the middle of a plain that was once far up in the mountains. The local landmark deserves a mention too — Rakhl-Ney, a tower that is almost the only building on the allod. The Council of Historians now sits in it. The tower itself is a grandiose library, with shelves the size of several houses. Of course, not only books are kept in Rakhl-Ney; there are plenty of artefacts of all kinds here as well. Besides the tower, the sights include an old system of portals leading to a great many allods. This was something like a crossroads where many magical paths of the June tribe converged… It is only a pity that many of the portals no longer work.

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's not to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Because the other day the personnel were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly forbidden to visit. Want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you do love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... Well, maybe in a low voice, in my ear.

Bosses: Hugger, Consumption, Rotgulp, Pandemician.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret base.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's so hard to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they meant to open the gates — I don't know, and where they did open them — I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the personnel were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. You want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... Well, unless it's in a low voice, in my ear.

Story allod:

In the Plagot Ruins, records were found of a temporal anomaly that Skrakan himself had studied. Finding the coordinates of the place was no problem, and the petty crook and thief Urri Miloslavin reported that at the indicated spot stood a Xadaganian base, which Catherina had allowed to be built in exchange for certain Imperial technologies. Intrigued by this base, the heroes set off there. And it turned out that Gates-II was the testing site of a Time Machine built by the Xadaganian genius Alex Everykin. And Alex was ready to travel far into the past — for instance, to see the world before the Cataclysm. But when a temporal portal was opened into Zayan's tower, the heroes and Miloslavin found themselves in the past, while the Zayan of the past ended up in the future, after which the portal closed. What had happened threatened temporal paradoxes, but the heroes managed to find a way back. To return back to the future, they had to use the Grain of Protopower... Alas, on returning and giving the Grain to Zayan, the heroes learned that it was precisely the Grain that Zayan had needed to stabilize the spell known as the Great Experiment. And its loss had caused the Cataclysm to happen. Still, a question remained — was what happened inevitable? And Gates-II did not escape the sad fate that awaited all the Imperial laboratories. No one will ever tell now exactly where the Imperial scholars decided to open a portal... But it is known that the island fell victim to a terrible plague. Was it Tep's plague? Or something even more terrible?

Bosses: Hugger, Consumption, Rotgulp, Pandemician.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

[Map missing]

Climate: Varied (tropical and wasteland): an oasis inside, the rest of the allod is rock.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by demons.

Story:

We arrive on the allod and, fighting our way through the demons into the dome, meet a Gibberling named Yodo (the master). The Master is indignant that we disturbed him, but decides to teach us great wisdom all the same. The first task he gives is to find the most beautiful, most special water lily. After a long search we return to the Master without having found it. He shares the wisdom that we would never have found it, for all lilies are special and beautiful — one need only notice their beauty. Then, to humble our pride, we must walk around every root of the Great Tree, and without hurrying. When we return to the Master, he wants to test us on Demons and orders us to kill three of each of the 3 kinds that live on the allod beyond the dome, but no more. After the victory over these demons, Yodo gives us a serious trial: to defeat two Demon Leaders, but no more. We defeat them. Yodo says that we are strong, but will we keep our balance on the edge between strength and wisdom? He gives us a last lesson: to kill the Great Demon — he is cunning, and we need to know how to deal with such creatures if they go on the attack against other allods. We overcome this demon too, and in parting Yodo says that we did well and learned wisdom — a pity it wasn't the wisdom he wanted to teach us.

Bosses: Demon Leader Scout, Demon Leader Warrior, Great Demon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: It reveals a little of the story of what befell this ancient allod after the events of the game series. The allod is dead. Or rather, almost all of its population, apart from the fauna, is dead. You arrive right at the camp of an Aviak and a Kanian woman, and each of these NPCs asks you to carry out a request. The first, the Aviak, lost close friends here and wants to recover their rings; the second has come on the orders of Nesmeyana, the new Great Mage of the allod of Umoir, and asks you to help her gather deadcaps. Deadcaps are mushrooms that grow all over the allod. Right up to 5.0 this was almost the only mention of Catherina (the second one was on the Coba Plateau). Amusingly, the mushroom-gathering storyline carried on on Umoir.

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod; before the undead curse it belonged to Kania.

Story:

We are met by the Kanian woman Vlasta Shukhova in a camp on the shore. She tells us that Catherina sent her to this allod to gather deathcap mushrooms, which she needs for a potion for speaking with the dead. According to her, they grow only here (actually they also grow in Jeer's Mansion). We agree to help her. Also in the camp is the aviak mercenary Daris. He complains that everything is bad: his sword broke, his comrades Amis, Atis and Potis died, a black raven flew past. He asks us to bring back the rings of his fallen comrades; he will carry them to his homeland. After we bring the deathcaps, Vlasta says that now we can overcome Fiercefang, who lives here; she makes a calming potion, and we are to use it when he goes berserk. In that state we would not defeat him. We find the first ring on Fiercefang. We find the second ring on a bunch of zombie warriors by a hut near the bridge (there is a chest of gold in it). We make our way into the settlement with the church, clearing out hordes of undead, and there we kill the Cursed Banshee Tear, and on her we pick up the last, third ring. In one of the huts is the Kanian necromancer Bolegost Mrakov. After the victory over him we pick up his diary. Judging by the entries, Bolegost, trying to save the island from a demon attack, decided to resort to an army of undead, made an elixir from deathcaps, but miscalculated the dose, went mad, and believed that the demons were still invading. It's a good thing we put an end to his madness. And we will send the diary to Umoir. We give it to Vlasta. "I'll pass this document on to the Umoir archive. If you ask me, this Bolegost is a hero! Just a poor unfortunate one."

Bosses: Fiercefang, Tear, Bolegost Mrakov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into Wolf Isle.

t:
The island of the Silent Hills always served me as proof that in the future we and the Kanians could live in peace. I didn't often go there, but when I did, I talked without fear to simple Kanians keeping their modest households, and stocked up on freshly baked, extraordinarily tasty bread. They didn't care about the feud between Tensess and Nezeb, or about the war between the League and the Empire...

Now ghosts hold sway there. As before, they go about their business: catching fish, hunting, grinding flour. And they were not at all glad to see either me or my crew. We barely got away.

I'm at a loss! What evil has appeared in the Silent Hills? Who cursed those poor people?

If you have the courage to take up the challenge of this riddle, follow my advice. Look for the cause of the Silent Hills' woes in the dark forest! The peasants always gave that place a wide berth. Perhaps one of them broke the age-old order and woke the evil slumbering there. Obstacles will surely stand in your way that you will have to overcome to reach the source of the evil. Remember that you will not be able to cleanse the island without fighting its ghostly inhabitants. That is the pain you will have to go through. Know that you bring them not death but deliverance from Darkness.

Bosses: Tsar Pike, Elder Miller, the Bane of Silent Hills.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The island of Silent Hills always served me as proof that in the future we and the Kanians will be able to live in peace. I didn't visit it often, but when I did, I talked without fear to simple Kanians tending their modest farms, and stocked up on their freshly baked, extraordinarily tasty bread. They didn't care a whit about the feud between Tensess and Nezeb, about the war between the League and the Empire... Now ghosts are the masters there. They go about their business as before: they fish, hunt, grind flour. And they were not at all glad to see either me or my crew. We barely got away. I am at a loss! What evil has appeared in Silent Hills? Who cursed the poor souls? If you have the courage to take up the challenge of this mystery, follow my advice. Look for the cause of Silent Hills' misfortunes in the dark forest! The peasants always gave that place a wide berth. Perhaps one of them broke the age-old order and woke the evil slumbering there. Obstacles will surely stand in your way, and you'll have to overcome them to reach the source of the evil. Remember that you won't manage to cleanse the island without fighting its ghostly inhabitants. That is the pain you'll have to go through. Know that you bring them not death, but release from the Darkness.

Bosses: Tsar Pike, Elder Miller, the Bane of Silent Hills.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: Bosses: Sylvan, Kodo the Silent and Nigan the Silent, Sentry, Veliyar.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by undead.

Story:

We arrive on the island, and a family of Seekers asks us for help. Lara, Indie and Nathan need to get into the tower for artifacts; to do so, several shards have to be collected and the sentry blocking the passage defeated. First we head into the thicket, where its inhabitants greet us aggressively; once we have cleared the thicket we find Sylvan, who complains that he will have to drive us off the allod himself. We defeat him, and Indie takes the shard. Next we make our way through the swamp, killing everyone who crosses our path, and reach the Silent Guard, who will not let us go further. Once they are defeated, Lara finds one more shard. We make our way through the ruins, again killing enemies. We find a passage, but it is guarded by the Sentry; we activate it and defeat it. After that the way into the Tower opens, and together with the Seeker family we defeat Veliyar. The gibberlings thank us for our help.

Bosses: Sylvan, Kodo the Silent and Nigan the Silent, Sentry, Veliyar.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: Bosses: Levoxia, Ligea, Cock Pit, Molpa.

Climate: Temperate. Closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by sirens.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Have you ever heard the legends about the beautiful singing of sirens that lures the ships of hapless sailors onto the reefs? Well — those aren't legends, but harsh reality. On one of the distant islands an elven tribe has settled — I can't bring myself to call that rabble anything else. Astronauts report that songs and music drift from Sirens' Rock containing some evil magic that makes the crew steer the ship straight to its doom. Resisting the magic is hard, but possible, if there is a talented specialist on board. Though some deaf bruiser will do just as well. The amount of shipwreck debris around the island speaks for itself. It's hard even to imagine how many honest sailors have fallen victim to those bloodthirsty creatures! And where are they now, what have those creatures done with them? Eaten them? I have, by the way, reports of undead sighted on the Rock... I advise you to avoid this island at any cost. Although, by rights, of course, it's long past time to send a squad of adepts there to mow that scum down from a safe distance.

Bosses: Levoxia, Cock Pit, Ligea, Molpa and the Demon of Madness.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Imperials love to boast of their technology and to play at conquering nature. That is why they placed one of their secret sanatoriums not just anywhere, but in the midst of the eternal ice. They found a suitable islet, frozen to its very core. They raised a dome there, and inside it built a fine, cozy little town. Outside the blizzard howls, but inside all is bliss — birds sing and the grass is green.

Only during construction they didn't take into account that a tribe of wild orcs lives in the caves under the dome. And that would have been fine, but in the course of the work they poured concrete over some important underground stream. Without water, first the mountain goats died, then the mushrooms in the caves dried up. The orcs went hungry and began coming out of the caves and attacking the sanatorium's guards. And the guards there are fierce — veterans to a man. The secrecy is of the highest level, which is why all outsiders are shot on the spot.

Bosses: Shakhrai-Gor, Pavel Syrin, Vyacheslav Lapochkin, Alexander Burdakin.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a holiday camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know, I know about that resort. The apotheosis of universal stupidity, not a resort. You know how scholars love to show off their technology and play at being conquerors of nature. Well, they took it into their heads to create a resort not just anywhere, but in the middle of the eternal ice. They found a suitable islet, freezing cold — terrible! They raised a dome there and built a whole little town under it. Imagine: all around a blizzard whistles, and inside the birds sing and the grass grows green... Bliss, in a word. Only our clever folk didn't take into account that a tribe of wild orcs lives in the caves there. They fed mainly on mountain goats and cave mushrooms. And when the engineers were building the dome, they sealed an underground stream in concrete. And the orcs were left with nothing at all to eat: the goats died off, the mushrooms withered. So they went to war with the resort's guards. And the guards there are first-rate, veterans to a man. No doubt they thought the big shots would be coming skiing. They made a great secret of it all — one step outside the perimeter and they shoot without warning. I wanted to unload some field rations from my hold for them, and they opened fire on me. Started blasting at an Imperial ship without a word! I barely got away. What secrets could they have there...

Bosses: Shakhrai-Gor, Pavel Syrin, Vyacheslav Lapochkin, Alexander Burdakin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Bosses: Rustle, Burian Jagger and Gurrian Jagger, Yarosvat Zoriev, Porfiry Polenov.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Al Rihat Ruins.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by renegade Kanian sorcerers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

The Workshop? Why yes, I've heard of it... It's a strange place, I tell you. And an evil one.

They say that sorcerers of every stripe used to gather there to practice their arts in peace and quiet. They practiced until they began experimenting on Sparks — capturing them by force and moving them into other bodies. A regular branch of Tep's Pyramid. Naturally, everyone turned against the sorcerers at once — both the League and the Empire. Only the sorcerers had no wish to abandon their experiments, and threw everyone who disagreed with them into the Astral. Ever since, sheer devilry has been going on on that island. Those who have flown past say the sorcerers started felling the forest and building wooden soldiers and golems. And — just think of it! — that whole wooden army has come to life and seems to be preparing to attack our allods. That's where experiments with Sparks lead.

Bosses: Rustle, Burian Jagger and Gurrian Jagger, Yarosvat Zoriev, Porfiry Polenov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Besides pirates, demons and anomalies, termites are sometimes encountered in the open astral. The senior members of your guild may still remember how, a couple of years ago, a large swarm of these insects appeared in the sky over Nezebgrad. The winged "guests" were promptly exterminated, after which scientists dissected several carcasses and found a logical explanation for the phenomenon. In the creatures' stomachs they discovered traces of meteorite dust — the best protection against the destructive effect of the astral.

Later many heroes rushed off in search of the colony to which the travelling termites belonged. For if one swarm made it, sooner or later others will follow! Better not to wait for disaster, but to find and destroy the royal nest.

Bosses: Ground Beetle, Murava, Itch, Chrysalis.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a termite nest.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do astronauts fear? Everyone knows: demons and anomalies. But recently another plague has appeared. One after another, battered ships came into port, and their crews told of swarms of termites flying through the Astral as if across a green lawn. Once such a swarm flew all the way to Nezebgrad itself! They were shot down, of course, while still on approach, but the question remained: how do these insects scurry about in a hostile medium that dissolves everything, living and non-living? I heard that a private merchant managed to catch a few specimens and dissect them. In the insects' abdomens he found traces of meteorite dust — that is what protected them! Now the Free Traders promise a tidy sum to anyone who finds the nest of these creatures. Many rushed off in search of it... Only, I fear, it is their own death they are searching for. Can you imagine how huge the termite mound must be? If I knew where it was — be there meteorite, gold or gems — I would give it a wide berth!

Bosses: Ground Beetle, Murava, Itch, Chrysalis.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

[Map missing]

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: League allod, a Gibberling settlement.

Story:

In the game the island had no NPCs. We arrive on the island at a makeshift pier, next to which is a mini-fort with astral cannons. Further on we see burning huts, and also books gathered in a pile and set on fire. The allod itself is a mountain, and the higher we climb along the paths, the more corpses of Gibberlings and Kanians we meet. At the very top stands the main hut; on the other side of the allod the houses are empty but not burned.

Bosses: no information.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Ah, so the rumours about this island have reached you too?

A mysterious place. An ancient June forge, now seized by the cultists of Tep. What goes on there, nobody knows. I heard of a group of desperate travellers who dared to make their way into the belly of the ancient volcano where the forge is located. Only one of them managed to return. According to him, Tep's cultists are trying to take control of the ancient June mechanisms and make them their loyal servants. If they succeed… June genius plus Tep's madness... Oh dear, oh dear... Be extremely careful if you dare to challenge this explosive mixture.

Bosses: Tep's Punisher, Tep's Rider, Dark Mistress, Shadow Devourer.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, so the rumours about that island have reached you too? A mysterious place. An ancient June forge, now seized by Tep's cultists. What goes on there, nobody knows. I heard of a group of desperate travellers who dared to penetrate the belly of the ancient volcano where the forge is located. Only one managed to come back. According to him, Tep's cultists are trying to take control of the ancient June mechanisms, to make them their loyal servants. If they succeed… The genius of the June plus the madness of Tep... Oh dear, oh dear... Be extremely careful if you dare to challenge this explosive mixture.

Bosses: Tep's Punisher, Tep's Rider, Dark Mistress, Shadow Devourer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Eljune.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a smugglers' lair.

Story:

We land near a Free Traders' camp. We are met by the Gibberlings of the Earthy Family. They say they are waiting for their mercenaries, who are supposed to kill the smugglers. They complain about them: they knock down prices and don't pay duties. This allod should be destroyed altogether, so that they don't gather here anymore. The allod is held together by meteorite iron, which we will have to steal. The next to ask us for help is Marat Vykhin. According to him, the ship with the mercenaries has been missing for a very long time, and they (the Free Traders) could be discovered and killed at any moment. He asks us to kill their chief, Kolotun the Forester, and then the rest will start fighting for power. The third, Khvoshch the Rowdy, says that they are out of money: he went into the forest to relieve himself and was spotted by the local Forestfolk. Now they are blackmailing the orc, saying that as long as he brings them a precious stone a day, they won't hand the traders over to the smugglers. In short, he asks us to deal with the Forestfolk and their chief, Barefoot. After clearing out the Forestfolk and the Camp, and also gathering the meteorite iron, we are thanked for our help. Khvoshch says that now the 10 sapphires they swindled out of him somehow have to be quietly slipped back to Marat, and asks us not to spread word of what happened.

Bosses: Forestfolk Chief Barefoot, Kolotun the Forester.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Desert, closest to the Dead Sea.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, an old Imperial base settled by orcs and goblins.

Story:

No sooner have we stepped off the ship than Tep's cultists attack us. After defeating them, we free a goblin named Sypun. He fearfully asks whether we are going to beat him. Once he is sure he is safe, he tells us about the situation on the allod. The goblin Zanud (the Supreme Shaman) declared these lands an independent goblin republic. They separated from the orcs, but then the water ran out. Since the water remained with the orcs, the goblins decided to attack them, but got a thrashing. Then "suicide men" appeared on the allod — that is what Zanud called Tep's cultists — and drove the orcs out. Now both the orcs and the goblins are on the verge of death because they have no water. The goblin sends us to their village to talk to Zanud. In short, Zanud didn't add many details; he only specified that the Cultists had seized the lake, the so-called Puddle, and won't let anyone near it; they are doing something there. We are asked to drive them out of there and to kill their chief — he sits in the former orc camp. The goblins will have water, and the orcs will fall before their might and beg the goblins to share the water. After the victory over the Shepherd, we find the orc woman Koryaga in a cage. She says that helping the foolish goblins is a bad idea: the Real locals are the Orcs; they stayed here to live after the night of astral portals, in the old Imperial camp. Their shaman Lysukha sent her to scout, but Koryaga was captured and so never found out what the cultists are looking for here. She asks us to intercept the punitive squad that has headed for the orcs and to kill their chief punisher. After the victory over the Commander, Lysukha thanks us for the rescue and says that before the orcs were driven out, the Commander tried to win them over to his side, saying they would restore Tep's power; she suggests we find and destroy the sources of Tep's power. In the old Zem ruins we find a mechanism; after activating it, the Shard of Tep appears, and we destroy it. After its destruction an orc woman crawls out of the sand and says that she hid and saw us destroy that thing; she thanks us, says she will tell Lysukha everything, and that we will be honored.

Bosses: Shepherd, Servant of Tep; Commander, Cultist of Tep; Shard of Tep.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: Bosses: Mamba, Capa, Twisthorn, Nastasya Zhmurova.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest fauna and an expedition camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Just a second, let me look in my notes. Hmm... Aha, here it is! An entry about a new island being added to the astral sailing directions, on which old June ruins were discovered. Right, right... In short, I know almost nothing about this island. It doesn't even have a name! According to our intelligence, a Kanian scout ship discovered, in the depths of the Astral, an island on which June ruins from the time of the rise of June civilization had survived. Since the ruins are of enormous scientific value, the League hastily sent a ship to the island with an archaeological expedition led by a certain Nastasya Zhmurova. The expedition reached the island and began excavating, after which contact with them was lost. The last message said that the scholars had almost broken through the passage to the central crypt of the June tomb. They also complained about kobolds that had turned up from who knows where. At present nothing is known of the expedition's fate. If you want my opinion — the scholars dug up what should not have been dug up. The thirst for knowledge, like the thirst for gain, leads to no good.

Bosses: Mamba, Capa, Twisthorn, Nastasya Zhmurova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Looking for treasure, are you? Heh-heh... There's no treasure there! Only sand, the scorching sun, heat, and scorpions nesting among the ruins.

As a Historian I know told me, there was once a huge observatory there, in which the June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars and compiled solar and lunar calendars and the most detailed horoscopes. And now all that's left of the temple-observatory are ruins half buried in sand.

And not long ago the Wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleared some of the halls, repaired the old battle golems and jealously guard the ruins against any intrusion. Their leader, who, as I understood, is called Mirage, desperately needs something in those ruins, and he will kill without hesitation anyone who enters beneath the vaults of the old temple. Luckily I got away in time, or my bones too would be drying in the hot desert sun now...

Bosses: Isides, Rattler, Horatrix, Mirage.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a haven of the Wormfaces.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Looking for treasure, are you? Heh-heh... There's no treasure there! Only sand, the blazing sun, heat and scorpions nesting among the ruins. As a Historian I know told me, there was once a huge observatory there, in which June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars and compiled solar and lunar calendars and the most detailed horoscopes. And now all that is left of the temple-observatory is ruins half-buried in sand. Not so long ago the Wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleared out some of the halls, repaired the old battle golems and jealously guard the ruins against any intrusion. Their leader, who I gather is called Mirage, desperately needs something in those ruins, and he will not hesitate to kill anyone who enters beneath the vaults of the old temple. Luckily I got away in time, or else my bones too would be drying in the hot desert sun now...

Bosses: Isides, Rattler, Horatrix, Mirage.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
If the idea of lazing about on sultry tropical shores doesn't appeal to you, we suggest you visit Triplefield! The Kanian town of Triplefield is a historical monument to the friendship of peoples! Here the Kanians and the elves of House de Doucer have long walked hand in hand, inspired by the brightest ideals. Forward — to a world of universal prosperity and Great Beauty!

Alas, the town's cultural and administrative center is currently closed owing to the war between werewolves and vampires. All the local elves of House de Doucer have turned into the latter. But never mind — in the south of the island the surviving Kanians have rebuilt a small village where you will surely be able to find a good guide.

During your journey around the island you can visit the enchanting enclave of the fallen elves. Their leader, Alister de Doucer, will receive you in his chambers and demonstrate the heights he has reached over long years in the art of training bats. His servants will consider it an honor to delight your ears with harp music and conversations about the beauty of twilight at this time of year.

Don't miss the chance to visit the ethnic community of werewolves, too. Only in the local cave can you hear songs performed by a moonlit choir of men and wolves. The pack leader, Mstislav Ferocious, will be glad to tell you old tales of grey wolves, and will also demonstrate stunts with fire in human and wolf form in turn!

Of course, it's worth seeing the part of the island once visited by the great Kanian inquisitor Alex Gordev. In the recent past this holy man wanted to rid the elves of the vampiric curse. The power of faith blazed brightly in his eyes, ready to burn away the corruption with one mighty blow of the Light... But something went wrong. Instead, the inquisitor himself turned into a terrifying undead, and the same fate befell all his guards.

Bosses: Alister de Doucer, Mstislav Ferocious, Milava Troepolskaya, Alex Gordev.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians and elves.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

An interesting little place. I haven't been there for a long while... And no wish to go, to be honest. Just a few years ago Triplefield was a lively trading town. What didn't they sell at the local market — elven gems, peasant bast shoes, Kanian armor... And then some disaster befell them: the dead rose and devoured the whole town, and few survived. The survivors brought down the only bridge leading to the town and settled in a small village some way off from the cursed ruins. Fortunately, the elves, whose enclave was nearby, were not affected by the curse that fell upon the town, and helped the surviving people set up at least some kind of peaceful life. But Triplefield will never see its former glory — now it's just a backwater hole. Still, I've heard that the League Church recently sent a squad of inquisitors there, and now I'm wondering — what could churchmen have lost in that Light-forsaken place?

Bosses: Alister de Doucer, Mstislav Ferocious, Milava Troepolskaya, Alex Gordev.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
There is an island in the Astral that can only be called an island with a stretch. On the one hand — big, well-shaped, there's even a little village nestled on it. On the other — it's not an allod at all, but a large floating turtle. The traveler never objected to her passengers, so they lived relatively well. Until recently.

They say the turtle island has been seized by demon worshippers. They have killed the local inhabitants and are trying to bend their drifting home to their evil will. And if they succeed, great trouble awaits the League and the Empire.

Bosses: Tikhon Yezhov, Hardshell, Gostemil Zalesky, Velerad Zalesky.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement seized by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You know about that one too? Hm... Strictly speaking, it isn't an island at all. It's a giant turtle that swims eternally through the astral. It's so enormous that a whole village lives on its back! Or rather, lived... Here's the thing... Two noblemen, the Zalesky brothers, mighty sorcerers, decided that the present authorities didn't suit them. They resolved to raise a revolt — for selfish reasons, of course. But Aidenus quickly learned of the treachery. The brothers gathered their retinue, loaded onto a ship and dashed off wherever their eyes led them. And their eyes spotted Turtle Island. They moored at the shore; the peasants saw the lordly ship and greeted the renegades with bread and salt, and in return the renegades put them to a cruel death! Only a few hunters managed to flee and hide in the astral. They were picked up by a Kanian ship belonging to my friend, Afanasy Nikitov. And he told me this story. As I understand it, the brothers are now trying to bend the flying turtle to their will. Can you imagine what will happen if they succeed? If someone sent those brothers to their graves, I'd have nothing but thanks for that hero!

Bosses: Tikhon Yezhov, Hardshell, Gostemil Zalesky, Velerad Zalesky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Bosses: Rattle, Ssera-Hay, Cau the Stormbringer, Tsol the Bloodstained Feather.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Jungles of Mboa-Mboa.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A real pearl of the Astral! An Imperial resort would look perfect in such a place. But, alas, we will have to give up those plans — hostile aborigines now live on the island. Originally only one tribe of aviaks lived in the lagoon. At one time we managed to develop minimal trade relations with them. Pure barter — their hides and precious stones in exchange for our weapons. Unheard-of generosity on our part, by the way! Everyone knows there are no weapons in the world better than ours. But a little later certain pirates, whose names we will never learn now, attacked the lagoon, hoping to easily steal all our goods. The aviaks repelled the attack and in revenge plundered the pirates' ship. There, apparently, they found unhatched eggs and took them under their care. Unfortunately, they were lizard eggs. As soon as they hatched, the whole brood ran away from the aviaks to the other end of the island. Soon a second tribe of aborigines appeared in the lagoon. And so one stunt by idiots who had got their hands on the Astral dealt the Empire a blow, a weak one, but a blow nonetheless. The aviaks of Tusky Lagoon now regard the "wingless" with utter contempt. If you fly past, expect no hospitality.

Bosses: Rattle, Ssera-Hay, Cau the Stormbringer, Tsol the Bloodstained Feather.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
The seasons... Once, before the Cataclysm, these words meant something more than just a change of dates on the calendar. The seasons followed one another without the help of mages, and there was nothing more constant in the whole world. But the old Sarnaut shattered into thousands of shards — and with it many of the orders of the old world vanished.

Bosses: Winter, Spring the Fair, Autumn the Woeful, Bright Summer.

Climate: Temperate; the climate on the shard is varied.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the dwelling place of the months and the seasons of the year.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The seasons... Long, long ago, when Sarnaut had not yet broken apart, these words meant more than a change of dates in the calendar. Nowadays, as they say, "spring is gone and summer's here, thanks to Yasker, never fear" — but back then the seasons changed on their own. Summer was followed by autumn, autumn by winter, then came spring and summer again. And so they went, one after another: one month decorously succeeding the other, neither lagging behind nor running ahead. But the Kanians have an old, old tale about a little girl who was lucky enough to see all twelve months at once! As if somewhere in the world there were a little grove where all twelve brother-months gathered once a year to discuss their year's doings. That's all old wives' tales, of course. Only a friend told me he had seen a strange islet in the far Astral. Like a glass ball, and inside it a grove with twelve fine young fellows. While they were flying past, the snow in the ball melted, grass peeped out, everything turned green and blossomed — and then in an instant turned yellow, withered, and the ground was dusted with snow again. They were just about to go closer, when — snap! — the island vanished as if it had never been. What do you think: maybe the tale told the truth? Maybe the brother-months are still alive, and that very grove is still intact?

Bosses: Winter, Spring the Fair, Autumn the Woeful, Bright Summer.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
For a long time nobody knew whether the Underwater Kingdom really existed, or whether it was just the invention of liars and dreamers telling tales of some tiny islet lost in the Astral with nothing on it but a wooden hut and a well.

At first glance it may seem there's nothing interesting there, and at second glance too. But it is precisely on this islet that the only entrance to the underwater kingdom of the sea lord lies. I wonder what riches are hidden beneath the depths?

Kanian skalds love to sing the song of a mighty sweet-voiced knight who not only visited the underwater city but was generously rewarded by the sea lord himself. Whether it was so or not, one can only guess. Or else visit the underwater kingdom and find out everything for yourself.

Bosses: Bereginya, Goldfeather Fish, Blackmarin, Sea King.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by underwater dwellers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Underwater Kingdom? To this day no one knows whether it really exists. I'm not in the habit of lying, so I'll tell you what I know myself. I heard this story from a Kanian merchant. His name was Sachkov, or maybe Sadkov. He was a rich merchant, he was friends with the Free Traders, and they say he even had his sights on becoming an Oligarch! He carried goods back and forth across the whole Astral and spent all his life on the road. His wife, clever and beautiful, saw her husband once every six months at best, but didn't complain. And one day Sadkov's ship happened to stray from the caravan route. He saw a small islet — not even an islet, just a scrap of land with a well and an abandoned hut. And the crew was just running out of water. They put in to shore, and Sadkov went to the well for a drink. No sooner had he bent over than a cold hand shot out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! And a muffled voice from under the water said: "Promise to give me what you have but do not know of, or else I'll drown you." Sadkov took fright and foolishly promised to give what he did not know of. If you don't know of it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, and when the merchant got home he began tearing his hair out. His wife met him right on the doorstep with a little baby. The merchant was seized with horror — he had promised his own child to the vile water spirit! But it's not for nothing that merchants are taught to count first and write only afterwards. Sadkov remembered that he had last been home more than a year ago, and the baby wasn't even a month old! His dearest spouse's debit and credit didn't tally — the child turned out to be someone else's. Sadkov threw his wayward wife and the child out of the house to go wherever they pleased, and gave his clerk, who had stayed behind to mind the business, a proper beating — the child looked a great deal like the clerk. And from then on the merchant drank himself into a stupor and drank away his whole fortune down to the last copper. And when the water spirit came for his due at the appointed time, the merchant advised him to look for his pledge himself, and paid out the interest on the loan in kicks and cuffs. That's the sad tale. If you see a small islet with a well in the Astral — don't be lazy, throw a keg of explosives down the well, so that the wretched water spirit who drives honest people into poverty won't find life a bed of roses!

Bosses: Bereginya, Goldfeather Fish, Blackmarin, Sea King.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Have you ever heard of the island of the Vortex?

A chunk of ice-bound earth floating in the astral. The grave of a Great Dragon that perished back in the days of the June. For many thousands of years its ghost has guarded its grave. Meanwhile, the depths of this island hold considerable deposits of meteorite iron. The Empire has a vital interest in seizing it. Perhaps you will manage to do it? Then remember this. To reach the ghost you will have to fight ice elementals, the wild yetis living in the cave, and the harpies guarding the passage to the Great Dragon's grave. Only once you are beside it will you be able to see the ghost and defeat it. Will you take it on?

Bosses: Yeti Tribal Chief, Vladimir Evdokimov, Ghost of the Great Dragon.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.
